entries.he: כְּעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה; וּכְאִלּוּ כּוֹפֵר בָּעִקָּר; וּכְאִלּוּ בָּא עַל עֲרָיוֹת כֻּלָּם; וּכְאִלּוּ בָּנָה בָּמָה; וּמִתְמַעֵט מֵחֲשִׁיבוּתוֹ וְאֵינֶנּוּ; וְרָאוּי לְגַדְּעוֹ כַּאֲשֵׁרָה; גַּם אֵין עֲפָרוֹ נִנְעֶרֶת; וּשְׁכִינָה מְיַלֶּלֶת עָלָיו.
entries.en: 25. An arrogant person will eventually commit adultery. He is like an idolater, like one who denies the essentials of faith, like one who committed all forms of incest, and like one who built an alter for idolatry. His importance diminishes to nothing, he deserves to be chopped down like the idolatrous Asherah tree. His remains will not be stirred for the resurrection and the Shechinah wails over him.

entries.he: גַּאֲוָה מְעַכֶּבֶת אֶת מָשִׁיחַ וּמַטְרִיד אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעוֹלָם.
entries.en: 40. The verse (Job 20:6): “If his height rises to the sky, and his head reaches the cloud(s) [he will be eternally destroyed like dung, those that look upon him will say, where is he?]”. And the verse (Proverbs 27:24): “For refuge is not forever, and is the crown (of wealth) lasting for generations?” are conducive to breaking haughtiness.

entries.he: הַפָּסוּק: "אִם יַעֲלֶה לַשָּׁמַיִם שִׂיאוֹ" (איוב כ, ו) וְהַפָּסוּק – "כִּי לֹא לְעוֹלָם חֹסֶן" (משלי כז, כד), הֵם מְסֻגָּלִים לְשַׁבֵּר אֶת הַגַּאֲוָה.
entries.en: 41. The verse, “Though his height ascends to the heavens” (Job 20:6), and the verse, “For strength does not endure forever” (Proverbs 27:24), are conducive to breaking arrogance.
